head.h1: Weekly Meal Prep vs a Full-Time Chef in Dubai — Real Prices and Timings

opening_paragraph: Here is the short answer. myCHEF weekly meal prep starts from AED 1,898 per week and gives you fresh, tailored meals cooked in batches on set days by a vetted chef. A full-time chef, by contrast, is a dedicated household hire who plans, shops and cooks fresh every day. Meal prep fits most families and busy professionals; a full-time chef fits high-frequency, fully bespoke households.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: When a Full-Time Private Chef Makes Sense
replace_in_block.new_heading: What employing a full-time chef commits you to
new_paragraphs: This is the part the cost comparison usually misses. A full-time chef is an employee, and UAE labour rules apply. Per the UAE government portal , normal private-sector hours are 8 hours a day or 48 hours a week under Article 17 of Federal Decree Law No. 33 of 2021, and Ramadan hours reduce by 2 daily. Overtime is capped at 2 hours a day and paid at base plus 25% , rising to 50% for work between 10pm and 4am. Anyone working five consecutive hours is owed at least 1 hour of breaks, which do not count as working time, and work on a scheduled rest day means a substitute day off or pay plus 50% .

Read that against a dinner-party schedule and the arithmetic changes. Evening service, weekend events and late clear-downs are exactly the hours that attract premiums, so a chef employed for family meals is not automatically available for your Friday night party at no extra cost. Weekly meal prep sidesteps the whole question: you buy delivered output instead of employed hours, with no overtime exposure and no rest-day calculation.
Is weekly meal prep cheaper than a full-time chef in Dubai?
Yes — weekly meal prep from AED 1,898 per week is far cheaper than a full-time chef, which costs a full monthly salary plus overheads. Meal prep wins unless you need daily cooked-to-order meals.
How much does weekly meal prep cost in Dubai?

Weekly meal prep costs from AED 1,898 per week, with a larger plan from AED 2,698 per week. The final price depends on people, meals per day and ingredient level; you approve it before cooking starts.
What is included in a weekly meal prep service?

A weekly meal prep service includes menu planning, grocery sourcing, in-home batch cooking on set days, and labelled, dated containers ready to reheat. Portions are weighed to your calorie or macro goals.
Can I find weekly meal prep near me across Dubai?

Yes — myCHEF provides weekly meal prep near you across all of Dubai, including Palm Jumeirah, Marina, Downtown, Jumeirah and Arabian Ranches. A vetted chef cooks in your own kitchen on your chosen days.
Is the meal prep menu customisable and halal?

The meal prep menu is fully customisable — keto, vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free and high-protein plans are all supported, and halal sourcing is standard. You approve every menu before each cooking day.
When is a full-time chef worth it instead of meal prep?

A full-time chef is worth it when you need daily, varied, cooked-to-order meals for a large household that entertains often. For most families and professionals, weekly meal prep is the better-value choice.
How do I get an exact quote?
Share your household size, meals per day and location with myCHEF and you will get an itemised proposal, usually within one business day.
Is it safe to meal prep a full seven days?
Not entirely chilled. Chilled food does not last a full week, so a seven-day plan means freezing the back half on the cooking day and thawing it as you go. Ask your chef what each dish holds for.
Is weekly meal prep healthy?
It is as healthy as the food in it. The controllable risks are storage and reheating rather than nutrition — reheat once until steaming, and never re-chill a warmed portion.

add_block.new_heading: What does weekly meal prep in Dubai include?
new_paragraphs: Weekly meal prep includes a professional chef cooking and portioning several days of meals in one or two visits, then leaving them labelled and ready to reheat. You get a menu built to your goals, groceries sourced, food safely chilled, and your kitchen left clean.

Most plans cover breakfasts, lunches and dinners across five to seven days, with snacks on request. Portions are weighed for calorie or macro targets, allergens are separated, and containers are dated so nothing is guessed. Because the chef batch-cooks, these meal-prep services cost far less per plate than daily cooking. It is the practical middle ground between takeaway fatigue and hiring a household chef — the fresh, home-cooked result without a full-time commitment.

add_block.new_heading: Weekly meal prep vs a full-time chef for families, fitness and corporate life
new_paragraphs: For most families the honest answer is weekly meal prep, because it solves the real problem — no time to cook — without the cost of a salaried hire. A full-time chef earns its place only when cooking demand is daily and varied.

Busy parents use meal prep to keep the fridge stocked with balanced dinners and school lunches. Fitness and wellness clients lean on it for consistent, weighed macros through a training block. Executives and dual-income couples use it to reclaim weeknights. A full-time private chef, by contrast, suits large households that entertain often, want every meal cooked to order, and need someone on hand for last-minute guests. Some corporate clients even blend the two — weekday meal prep for the household, a private chef booked for the occasional dinner.

Most Dubai households land on weekly meal prep and only move to a full-time chef when entertaining becomes near-constant. add_block.new_heading: Is it okay to meal prep for a week?
new_paragraphs: Partly, and the limit is storage rather than cooking. Chilled storage is the limit, not the cooking. A genuine 7 day meal plan means part of the week chilled and the remainder frozen on the cooking day, then thawed as the week goes on. Anyone offering seven days of fridge-fresh food is either cooking twice in the week or ignoring the chill rule.

That is also the honest answer to whether weekly meal prep is healthy: it is exactly as healthy as what goes into it, and the real risk is storage rather than nutrition. Reheat a portion once, until it is steaming throughout, and do not re-chill something you have already warmed. Those two habits matter more to a week of batch-cooked food than any ingredient choice.
Why meal prep is bad, in the cases where it is

The case against is worth stating plainly, because it is real. Texture degrades unevenly — rice and roasted vegetables hold, fried food and dressed leaves do not. Variety drops, and by day four most people stop wanting the thing they chose enthusiastically on Sunday. And a plan built for a good week tends to collapse in a bad one, which is when takeaway wins. A full-time chef solves that by cooking to the day you are actually having; meal prep solves cost and predictability instead.
Good weekly meal prep ideas, and prep aimed at weight loss

Good weekly meal prep ideas share a structure rather than a recipe: one protein, two vegetables, one starch, and sauces kept in separate containers so a portion can be changed without recooking it. Healthy meal prep ideas for the week follow from the method — grilled and steamed items reheat far better than fried ones, and they survive four days without turning to paste.

Meal prep ideas for weight loss use the same structure with portions weighed rather than judged by eye, which is the variable most people misjudge at home. A 7 day meal prep for weight loss, or any weekly meal prep for weight loss, works on portion control and consistency, not on a special ingredient. Neither a meal prep service nor myCHEF sets those targets: that is a matter for your coach or a dietitian, and a caterer promising a result is selling something it cannot evidence.
